title: Nvidia AI chip share in China falls as Huawei catches up
source_used: Yahoo Finance (TIKR commentary relaying the Reuters report on the IDC data); the Investing.com page returns HTTP 403
key_facts: IDC report seen by Reuters: Nvidia's share of China's data-centre AI chip market fell to 34% in January to June 2026.
Nvidia shipped 678,000 AI accelerators to China in the period, down 44% year on year; Huawei shipped 572,000, up from more than 300,000, for a 28% share.
Alibaba's T-Head holds 7%, Cambricon 5%, Baidu's Kunlunxin 4% and Hygon 3%; nine of the 11 Chinese chipmakers IDC tracks shipped more than a year ago.
GPU shipments fell 26% to 991,000 units while other AI accelerators rose nearly 80% to 1.016 million and now outnumber GPUs.
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang says the US export curbs forced a US company to hand China's $50 billion AI chip market to Huawei; Nvidia did not respond to Reuters' request for comment.

Per the Yahoo commentary, Nvidia said on its August earnings call that it shipped less than 1% of data-centre revenue in H200 products to China and that its forward outlook has no China data-centre compute revenue.
IDC expects total accelerator shipments in China to grow 19% this year while GPU shipments fall 9%.
quote_evidence: Nvidia's (NVDA:NASDAQ) share of China's data-center AI chip market fell to 34% in the first half of 2026, according to an IDC report Reuters accessed.
Nvidia shipped 678,000 AI accelerators to China from January to June, down 44% from the same period last year.
He says they forced a US company to hand China's $50 billion AI chip market to Huawei.
why_it_matters_hint: US export controls are shrinking Nvidia's China share while Huawei and other local makers gain.
event_date: first half of 2026 (IDC report; Reuters story of 13 Oct 2026)
